verdict: MercadoLibre grew revenue 45% to $10.8B as shoppers bought more often and Mercado Pago handled $109B of payments, while spending on free shipping and new warehouses held operating profit to $676M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Net revenues & financial income of $10.8B vs $7.4B in Q3 2025, in dollars; up 41% ignoring currency moves

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Diluted earnings per share, vs $8.32 a year ago; net income was $448M

kpis.label: Gross merchandise volume
kpis.note: The total value of goods sold on the marketplace (GMV), up 38% in dollars; 94 million unique buyers, up 22%

kpis.label: Total payment volume
kpis.note: The total value of payments processed by Mercado Pago (TPV), up 53% in dollars; 93 million monthly fintech users

segments.name: Commerce
segments.note: Marketplace fees, shipping, first-party product sales, advertising and MELI+ subscriptions.

segments.name: Fintech
segments.note: Mercado Pago payment fees, financing fees and interest earned on consumer and merchant credit, plus point-of-sale devices.

opex.name: Product and technology development
opex.note: Building and running the marketplace, payments platform and AI tools.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Advertising and customer acquisition, including a bigger affiliates program push in Brazil.

opex.name: Provision for doubtful accounts
opex.note: Money set aside for loans and credit-card balances that may not be repaid, as the credit book grows.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Staff and running the company, including hiring tied to new fulfillment capacity.

takeaways.title: Growth stayed very fast
takeaways.text: Revenue reached $10,750M, up 45% in dollars and 41% ignoring currency moves, with Brazil the strongest of the big markets. Commerce revenue rose 47% in dollars and Fintech 42%, so both halves of the business grew at a similar pace.

takeaways.title: Margin was spent on purpose
takeaways.text: Income from operations fell 6% to $676M, a 6.3% margin, as more free shipping, new fulfillment space added ahead of peak season and extra affiliate marketing in Brazil cost more than they returned this quarter. Net income still rose 6% to $448M on a lower tax bill and smaller currency losses.

takeaways.title: The credit book keeps scaling
takeaways.text: The credit portfolio reached almost $18B, up 62% year over year, with credit cards now 47% of it. Late loans stayed contained — the 15–90 day non-performing ratio was 7.0%, broadly stable and close to all-time lows — while the lending spread after losses (NIMAL) was 20.1%.

otherDetail: Below operating income, $55M of interest income and other financial gains was more than offset by $58M of interest expense and other financial losses and $72M of foreign-currency losses, for a net other expense of $75M.
footerNote: MercadoLibre reports 'net revenues and financial income' — marketplace sales plus Mercado Pago's financial income; its cost line includes financial expenses.
